Glutes exercise

Hip Thrust

The hip thrust loads the glutes directly in their strongest, most shortened position. It is easy to learn, easy to load heavily and one of the best isolation-style exercises for glute size and strength.

By Khushi Gupta · Reviewed October 2026

Primary
Glutes
Also works
Hamstrings, Quads, Adductors, Core
Equipment
Barbell, bench, bar pad
Level
Beginner

How to do it

  1. Sit on the floor with your upper back against the edge of a bench, roughly at the bottom of your shoulder blades.
  2. Roll a padded barbell over your legs until it sits in the crease of your hips.
  3. Plant your feet flat, about hip width, so that at the top your shins will be vertical.
  4. Tuck your chin slightly and brace your abs so your ribs stay down.
  5. Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
  6. Pause for a second at the top with your glutes fully contracted.
  7. Lower your hips under control until they are just above the floor, then repeat.

Coaching cues

  • Chin tucked, eyes forward
  • Ribs down, pelvis tucked at the top
  • Shins vertical at lockout
  • Push through the heels
Advertisements

Common mistakes and fixes

Arching the lower back at the top

Finish with a slight posterior pelvic tilt and ribs down. The movement stops when your hips are fully extended.

Feet too far forward or too close

Feet too far forward shifts work to the hamstrings, too close to the quads. Adjust until your shins are vertical at the top.

Head thrown back, looking at the ceiling

Keep your gaze forward and let your torso pivot around the bench.

Skipping the pause

Hold the top for one to two seconds. That is where the glutes work hardest.

Sets and reps

GoalPrescription
Strength3-4 sets of 5-8 reps, 2-3 minutes rest
Hypertrophy3-4 sets of 8-15 reps, 90 seconds rest
Beginner3 sets of 10-12 glute bridges, then progress to the bench

Pick a starting weight with the one rep max calculator, and load the bar with the plate calculator.

Variations

  • Glute bridge Done from the floor with a shorter range; good for beginners and home training.
  • Single-leg hip thrust Bodyweight or light load, one side at a time.
  • Machine hip thrust Faster setup and easier to load.
  • Banded hip thrust A band around the knees adds more glute med work.

Muscles worked

The gluteus maximus is the prime mover, extending the hip against the bar. Muscle activity studies consistently show high glute activation in the hip thrust, peaking at the top of the rep.

The hamstrings, quads and adductors assist, and the abs hold your pelvis in position.

Benefits

Because the hip thrust places little load on the spine and needs almost no technique, you can train it close to failure safely. That makes it an efficient accessory alongside squats and RDLs, which load the glutes in a stretched position.

Stronger glutes support sprinting, jumping and a healthy lower back.

Safety and who should modify it

Always use a bar pad or folded mat across your hips. If the bench slides, put it against a wall. Anyone with hip pain can start with bodyweight glute bridges and progress gradually.

Frequently asked questions

Hip thrust or squat for glutes?

Use both. Squats load the glutes in a deep stretch, hip thrusts in a full contraction. Together they cover the whole range.

How high should the bench be?

Around 40 to 45 cm (16 to 18 in) works for most people. The edge should sit just below your shoulder blades.

Why do I feel hip thrusts in my hamstrings?

Your feet are probably too far from your body. Bring them closer until your shins are vertical at the top.
